result.summary: Bracken Spark Services (Rian Sol) has offered 29 Sep after 15:00, which is one of the tenant's slots. I assigned him, confirmed the slot with him and the tenant, and asked him to come earlier if he can. The downstairs light flickers and pops, which may be a wiring fault, and the landlord has never approved work on it. I escalated it as a high-priority safety risk and queued a call to the landlord for approval. The same call asks who owns the TV. I also asked the tenant whether the rear door still shuts and locks, since the handle has come off.

judgement.why_this_decision: Ev 19 gives a slot that matches ev 16, so the visit can be scheduled. The landlord's 'Please sort it' (ev 3) only answered the TV request (ev 2). The light was added later (ev 5) and never approved. A light that flickers and pops may mean arcing. Jev rated it an emergency-level safety risk (0.88), so I escalated with high priority before assigning without approval for the light. The landlord's 'I don't remember leaving a TV' means the TV may be the tenant's. So I limited the electrician to assessing it and asked the landlord to confirm ownership before any repair or disposal cost goes to him. The rear-door handle (ev 15, 18) could leave the property insecure, so I asked the tenant whether the door still locks.

alternatives_considered.option: Just confirm 29 Sep and carry on
alternatives_considered.why_not: The light has never been approved, and popping is a possible safety risk that should be escalated and put to the landlord. The TV ownership question also has cost consequences.

alternatives_considered.option: Hold the whole visit until the landlord answers
alternatives_considered.why_not: The landlord was away (ev 7). The TV attendance is approved and the light is a safety concern, so stalling would leave the risk in place.
Ownership is unconfirmed and the landlord gave no disposal instruction (ev 4).

alternatives_considered.option: Open a lock or handyman job now
alternatives_considered.why_not: I don't yet know whether the door still secures, so I asked the tenant first.
